summary: Toulouse Climate Check is an interactive, browser-based prototype that visualizes annual air temperature changes near Toulouse from 1991 to 2025 by leveraging NASA POWER data. Utilizing linear regression against a 1991–2020 reference average, the tool calculates and displays a statistically significant local warming trend of +0.41 °C per decade. Built with standard web technologies and OpenAI Codex assistance, the project translates complex MERRA-2 datasets into clear, accessible graphics for the general public. By making this raw data visually readable for everyday people, the ultimate goal is to raise local awareness about the concrete reality of global warming, all while transparently acknowledging the statistical limitations of the model.
details:
High-Level Project Summary
Toulouse Climate Check is a small interactive tool that explores annual air temperature near Toulouse from 1991 to 2025 using NASA POWER data. It shows each year's difference from the 1991–2020 average and fits a linear trend. The estimated change is +0.41 °C per decade. A simple confidence interval indicates that this trend is statistically significant under the stated regression assumptions.

Detailed Project Description
Our browser-based prototype displays 35 annual estimates of air temperature at 2 metres for one NASA POWER grid point near Toulouse. Users can switch between absolute temperature and differences from the 1991–2020 reference average, then select a year to inspect its value. We fit a linear regression to quantify the change over time. The estimated slope is +0.41 °C per decade, with a conventional 95% confidence interval from +0.19 to +0.64 °C per decade. Since this interval excludes zero, the result is significant under the assumptions of this simple model. The tool works offline. Its scope is limited to one location and variable; we have not fully assessed serial dependence, model uncertainty or the choice of period.

Use of Super Intelligence (SI)

OpenAI Codex assisted with the prototype concept, code, presentation and verification of calculations. The temperature data came from NASA POWER.

NASA Data
We used NASA POWER Monthly and Annual Point API data for the parameter T2M: annual mean air temperature at 2 metres, derived from MERRA-2, at 43.6° N and 1.44° E for 1991–2025. We used the annual ANN values from the CSV. Source: https://power.larc.nasa.gov/api/temporal/monthly/point?parameters=T2M&community=AG&longitude=1.44&latitude=43.6&format=CSV&start=1991&end=2025

Space Agency Partner Data and Other References
No additional space agency dataset was used. Other resources: NASA POWER API documentation (https://power.larc.nasa.gov/docs/services/api/temporal/monthly/); NIST guidance on linear regression confidence intervals (https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/software/dataplot/refman1/auxillar/olp_fit.htm); Python, HTML, CSS and JavaScript; OpenAI Codex assistance as disclosed above.
